The first respondent before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis is the appellant herein.

This appeal has been filed against the judgment and decree dated 31.07.2006 made in M.C.O.P.No.109 of 2003, on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Salem / Additional District Court cum Special Court (Essential Commodities Act) Salem.
P.Subramani vs Chennammal on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85016962/
1 2.The brief facts of the case is that on 15.06.2002 at about 4.45 hours, the deceased Jothi Prakash travelled in a Tractor bearing Registration No.MDO 7958 as a non fare paying passenger in Pallathur Kambainallur Road, near Narayanan Land.

entities.text:
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Salem / Additional District Court cum Special Court (Essential Commodities Act) Salem
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: At that time, the driver of the Tractor drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the stone revertment on the Northern side of the Oni, due to which, the Tractor capsized and the deceased Jothi Prakash died on the spot.
3.Thereafter, the wife of the deceased Jothi Prakash/ first respondent filed claim petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.15 Lakhs.

After adjudication, the Tribunal, awarded a sum of Rs.2 Lakhs as compensation to the claimant/ first respondent and third respondent and directed that the appellant and second respondent to jointly and severally pay the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis compensation along with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization and proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the same, the appellant / owner of the vehicle has filed this appeal.
4.The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that there are two wives for the deceased namely, respondents 1 and 3.

The third respondent has already filed M.C.O.P.No.174 of 2003 before the Principal Subordinate Court, Dharmapuri and the learned Principal Sub Judge has already passed award in her favour vide order dated 27.02.2006.

Similarly, the first respondent filed M.C.O.P.No.109 of 2003, on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Salem / Additional District Court cum Special Court (Essential Commodities Act) Salem, however, the appellant was not able to produce the order passed in M.C.O.P.No.174 of 2003 before the Tribunal and the impugned award came to be passed.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Salem / Additional District Court cum Special Court (Essential Commodities Act) Salem
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Hence, this Court may set aside the impugned award and remand the matter back to the Tribunal so as to enable the appellant as well as the third respondent to produce the award passed in M.C.O.P.No.174 of 2003 for appropriate adjudication.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.The learned counsel appearing for the third respondent raise no serious objection.
6.The learned counsel appearing for the first respondent vehemently opposed and submitted that the first respondent is the wife of the deceased Jothi Prakash and she is entitled to claim compensation as against the owner of the vehicle, in which, the alleged second wife/ third respondent or the appellant should have no grievance.
7.Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant, learned counsel appearing for the first respondent as well as the learned counsel appearing for the third respondent and perused the materials available on record.
8.The facts in the present case is not in dispute.
The two wives of the deceased claim compensation for the death of the deceased.

The third respondent has already filed M.C.O.P.No.174 of 2003 before the Principal Subordinate Court, Dharmapuri and the learned Principal Sub Judge has already passed award in her favour vide order dated 27.02.2006.

However, that award was not produced P.Subramani vs Chennammal on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85016962/
2 before the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Tribunal and hence the impugned award came to be passed.
